title: Tesla Is Building a Robotaxi for Wheelchair Users!
summary:
Great news! Tesla is building a self-driving car that wheelchair users can use. A Tesla representative told lawmakers in Washington, D.C., on Monday that the company is working on a "purpose-built, wheelchair-accessible autonomous vehicle." That means a car that drives itself and is designed so people in wheelchairs can get in and out easily.

Right now, Tesla has a small fleet of self-driving cars in Texas cities like Austin, Dallas, and Houston, and also in Miami, Florida. But those cars are Tesla Model Ys, which are not wheelchair accessible. Tesla also makes a special self-driving car called the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals, but it's not wheelchair accessible either.

No robotaxi company in the U.S. currently offers driverless rides that are fully wheelchair accessible. Waymo, the biggest robotaxi company, says they haven't found a vehicle that works with their technology and is also wheelchair accessible. Another company, May Mobility, offers wheelchair-accessible rides, but they have a human driver on board to help with ramps.

The Americans With Disabilities Act says companies can't discriminate against people with disabilities. Some cities require ride-hailing companies to offer wheelchair-accessible services. In 2025, the U.S. government sued Uber for not doing enough for riders with disabilities.

Tesla hasn't said when the wheelchair-accessible robotaxi will be ready. The company often takes years to build new products. But it's exciting that they're working on it! Imagine being able to call a self-driving car that anyone can use, no matter how they get around.
why_it_matters: If Tesla succeeds, kids and adults who use wheelchairs could travel independently, making the world more fair and opening up new possibilities for everyone.

background_read: The Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) is a civil rights law passed in 1990 that requires buildings, transportation, and services to be accessible to people with disabilities.
Waymo, a self-driving car company owned by Alphabet (Google's parent), has been testing driverless taxis in cities like Phoenix, Arizona.
In 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice sued Uber, saying the company didn't provide enough wheelchair-accessible rides, leading to a settlement to improve services.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tesla, the electric car company, and its representative talking to lawmakers.
WHAT: Tesla is developing a self-driving car specifically designed for wheelchair users, a first for the robotaxi industry.
WHERE: Announcement in Washington, D.C., with operations in Texas and Florida.
WHY: To include people with disabilities in driverless transportation and follow laws that require equal access.

They believe a special robotaxi can open new markets and show that self-driving cars can work for everyone.
